description: Verify two scientific claims against real abstracts: one is supported, one is contradicted, and one paper is unrelated. Cite the evidence for each verdict.
task_prompt:
Two claims are under review.
Claim 1: High levels of CRP reduces the risk of exacerbations in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
Claim 2: Low nucleosome occupancy correlates with high methylation levels across species.
Using the papers in documents/, decide for each claim whether the evidence supports or contradicts it. Write each verdict on its own line as 'Claim N: SUPPORTED' or 'Claim N: CONTRADICTED'. For each verdict, cite the paper and the specific result behind it.

seeds.text: Low nucleosome occupancy correlates with high methylation levels across species.
rationale: Clustered methylation occurs at unprecedented densities and directly disfavors nucleosomes, contributing to nucleosome positioning between clusters.

seeds.text: High levels of CRP reduces the risk of exacerbations in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
rationale: In the first year of follow-up, multivariable-adjusted odds ratios for having frequent exacerbations were 1.2 (95% CI, 0.7-2.2; 17 events/1000 person-years) for individuals with 1 high biomarker, 1.7 (95% CI, 0.9-3.2; 32 events/1000 person-years) for individuals with 2 high biomarkers, and 3.7 (95% CI, 1.9-7.4; 81 events/1000 person-years) for individuals with 3 high biomarkers compared with individuals who had no elevated biomarkers (9 events/1000 person-years; trend: P = 2 × 10(-5)).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE Simultaneously elevated levels of CRP and fibrinogen and leukocyte count in individuals with COPD were associated with increased risk of having exacerbations, even in those with milder COPD and in those without previous exacerbations.

claim_2_verdict.description: Claim 2 is supported by the evidence
claim_2_verdict.claim: Low nucleosome occupancy correlates with high methylation levels across species.

claim_1_verdict.description: Claim 1 is contradicted by the evidence
claim_1_verdict.claim: High levels of CRP reduces the risk of exacerbations in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

tool_result.alt_conclusion: Taken together, these results support the claim that high levels of CRP reduces the risk of exacerbations in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
